title: Telemetry-driven prefill orchestrator and v3 compatibility smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: After upstreaming FlashAttention v3 support we observed intermittent latency spikes on 1-3% of long-context requests during cold startup and aggressive prefilling. Investigation suggests a combination of (a) kernel choice oscillation during prefill vs decode phases, (b) suboptimal workspace allocation for some sequence-length buckets, and (c) jitter in the kernel prober that triggers fallback thrashing.

Goal: Build a telemetry-driven prefill orchestrator that (1) stabilizes kernel selection across prefill->decode transitions, (2) smooths v3 adoption with staged compatibility heuristics, and (3) exposes signal thresholds to the runtime and Console for rapid rollbacks. The orchestrator should reduce post-deploy latency tail by >=30% for affected workloads and provide safe canary controls.
acceptance_criteria: Design and implement a prefill orchestrator component in the runtime that consults recent kernel telemetry before selecting a kernel for new prefill requests
Telemetry rules (examples provided) are available in Console and default to conservative v2-first for the first 48h of rollout, then enable v3 for stable buckets
End-to-end canary plan: 5% traffic for 24h, automated rollback on 10% increase in p95 latency or 5% error delta
Observed reduction of p99 startup spikes in the synthetic long-context test harness by >=20% compared to baseline v3 rollout without orchestrator
Runbook documenting debug steps, telemetry queries, and temporary toggles for emergency rollback
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Spike repro harness added to perf-lab. Reproduced 1.8x p95 increase on 8k+ contexts during prefill handshake when v3 kernels were chosen mid-prefill.

2026-03-07: Telemetry schema extended to include kernel_choice, kernel_version, workspace_size_requested, workspace_size_granted, input_shape_bucket, prefiller_id. New metrics names prefiller.kernel_choice and runtime.kernel_handoff_count.

2026-03-08: Early design review with runtime and infra teams. Decided on a lightweight orchestrator in the serving process (avoid separate control plane RTT). Will use a short LRU cache of recent kernel stability scores per (model, shape_bucket) computed from telemetry windows.

2026-03-09: Implemented kernel stability scorer and prober backoff. Scorer favors kernels with low observed decode-jitter and low handoff_count. Prober will sample <2% of requests for alternate kernel probing during canary.

2026-03-10: Found regression scenario where v3 kernel reports lower average latency but higher variance for microbatch sizes <4 due to workspace fragmentation. Added microbatch-aware heuristic to prefer v2 for batch_size <=3 unless v3 stability score > 0.95.

2026-03-11: Integration test discovered memory reclamation corner-case when toggling kernels rapidly. Added a 200ms soft-quarantine window after kernel switch to avoid immediate reprobing on the same prefill session.
2026-03-12: Canary plan drafted: phased rollout with Console knobs, initial 1% traffic for 6h, then 5% for 24h with automated SLO guardrails. Ops runbook and rollback script stubbed.

2026-03-13: Benchmarks from perf-lab: synthetic long-context job p95 improved by 28% vs naive v3 rollout; p99 improved by 18%. Still seeing a tail for shapes with workspace > 120MB; added mitigation task to explore tiling and workspace reuse (follow-up ticket).
test_plan: Unit tests for stability scorer logic and prober sampling randomness (deterministic seed coverage)
End-to-end perf-lab job: 100k synthetic prefill->decode flows across shapes [512, 2k, 8k, 16k], compare baseline (v2-only), naive-v3, and orchestrator-v3 runs
Chaos test: force kernel-allocation-failure and verify orchestrator falls back without leaking buffers
Canary on staging with traffic replay from production traces for 48h
Post-deploy monitoring dashboard with prefiller.kernel_choice, kernel_handoff_count, p95/p99 latency by shape_bucket, workspace_granted_ratio

notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: keeping orchestrator local avoids control plane latency but increases runtime binary complexity. Chosen local approach to meet 50ms SLOs for prefill decision path.
Tradeoff: conservative default (v2-first for 48h) slows v3 ramp for some high-throughput shapes, but reduces early customer exposure to instability.

Open question: should we persist kernel stability scores across restarts? Current plan keeps scores in a short in-memory LRU to avoid staleness; persisting would help reboots but adds state migration complexity.
Follow-up: create ENG-430778 to evaluate workspace tiling and fragmentation fixes tied to v3 allocator improvements.
